title: Prime Palindrome
summary: Given an integer n , return the smallest integer that is both a prime number and a palindrome, and is greater than or equal to n .
statement: Given an integer n , return the smallest integer that is both a prime number and a palindrome, and is greater than or equal to n . Note that 1 is not a prime number, and a palindrome reads the same forwards and backwards.
constraints: Return the smallest prime palindrome at least n.
hints: Except eleven, every even-length palindrome is divisible by eleven, so generate odd-length palindromes.
Mirror numeric prefixes and primality-test candidates in increasing length/order.
Handle 8..11, mirror prefix without its last digit, and return first candidate>=n that is prime.
Prefix order equals palindrome order, while the divisibility fact safely removes all other even lengths.
editorial: Prefix order equals palindrome order, while the divisibility fact safely removes all other even lengths.

tests.explanation: Seven is the first prime palindrome no smaller than six.
